column3: The Hebrew explicitly names Israel before “all who” and says “all the wars of Canaan.”
The Hebrew repeats “only” and does not explicitly call the generations “subsequent.”
The Hebrew uses singular collective names for the Canaanite, Sidonian, and Hivite.
The Hebrew says “through the hand of Moses.”
The Hebrew uses singular collective names for all six peoples.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew retains the image “in the eyes of the LORD.”
The Hebrew repeats Cushan-rishathaim’s name where BSB has “him.”
The Hebrew repeats “the sons of Israel” and the LORD’s name; it separately narrates the deliverance instead of expressing it only as purpose.
The Hebrew says he judged Israel rather than became its judge. It leaves his hand’s owner unnamed, repeats Cushan-rishathaim, and says “his hand prevailed.”
The Hebrew joins the forty years of rest and Othniel’s death with “and,” rather than “until.”
The Hebrew explicitly repeats the LORD as the one strengthening Eglon.
The Hebrew begins with an unnamed “he,” coordinates gathering and attacking, and ends with a plural verb for taking possession.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names the Israelites twice and the LORD twice; Ehud is described as restricted in his right hand.
The Hebrew calls the sword’s edges “two mouths” and uses plural “his garments.”
The Hebrew explicitly repeats Eglon and calls him “a very fat man.”
The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed and repeats “the tribute.”
The Hebrew leaves the person ordering silence unnamed and describes the departing men as those standing by him.
The Hebrew leaves the seated man unnamed rather than repeating “the king.”
The Hebrew refers to the victim with “his belly”; BSB explicitly names Eglon.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “the blade” when describing the fat closing around it.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses pronouns instead of repeating Ehud and Eglon and retains the image of covering his feet.
The Hebrew describes waiting until shame; BSB has becoming worried.
The Hebrew leaves those delaying unnamed; BSB explicitly names the servants.
The Hebrew does not explicitly name Seirah here and says “he was before them”; BSB interprets this as becoming their leader.
The Hebrew names singular collective Moab; BSB uses plural “Moabites.”
The Hebrew names Moab, not plural Moabites, and describes “every stout one and every man of valor.”
Close to the Hebrew.
